name: Product gross margin
expression: (Product price − matching product cost) / product price
units: fraction; multiply by 100 for percentage display
inputs: Product price: revenue per unit on a stated basis.
Matching product cost: the corresponding cost basis, consistently defined.
scope: Price must be nonzero. State whether discounts and other price adjustments are included; this gross measure is not final net profit.
status: Clarified units and matching cost basis

name: Convert fractional markup to margin
inputs: Markup: (price − cost) / cost, entered as a decimal, e.g. 25% = 0.25.
scope: Use consistent price and cost bases with positive cost and price. The source’s neighboring percentage formulas must be converted to decimal fractions first. A markup of −1 makes this conversion undefined.

name: Product markup
expression: (Product price − matching product cost) / matching product cost
units: fraction; multiply by 100 for percentage display
inputs: Product price: the corresponding selling price per unit.
Matching product cost: the same cost definition used in gross profit.
scope: Cost must be nonzero. Markup is measured relative to cost, unlike margin measured relative to revenue.

name: Convert fractional margin to markup
inputs: Margin: (price − cost) / price, entered as a decimal, e.g. 20% = 0.20.
scope: Use consistent positive price/cost bases. A margin of 1 makes this conversion undefined. Do not enter 20 when the intended fraction is 0.20.

name: Net present value: complete cash-flow form
inputs: CFₜ: incremental net cash flow at time t, including the initial investment as a negative flow when appropriate.
r: compatible per-period discount rate.
T: defined valuation horizon.
scope: The source’s “inflows − outflows” must be discounted at their respective times. Match currency, timing and risk assumptions; a positive scenario NPV is not a guarantee of realized profitability.

name: Internal rate of return: cash-flow definition
expression: Find r such that Σₜ₌₀ᵀ CFₜ / (1 + r)ᵗ = 0
inputs: CFₜ: the complete dated series of net cash flows, including investment outflows.
r: the candidate periodic internal rate of return.
scope: The source uses “NPB” and a single-inflow form. IRR requires a defined cash-flow series; nonconventional patterns can produce multiple or no meaningful IRRs. A normal initial outflow followed by inflows contains both signs and is not automatically invalid. Compare scale and NPV rather than ranking every project solely by IRR.
status: Corrected typo and completed multi-period definition

name: Simple payback: level annual inflows
expression: Initial investment / annual positive net cash inflow
inputs: Initial investment: the positive amount to recover.
Annual positive net cash inflow: equal net inflow in each year.
scope: This shortcut assumes level inflows and does not discount them or count cash flows after recovery. Uneven inflows require a cumulative cash-flow schedule; the source does not supply one.

name: Profitability index: initial-outlay convention
expression: Present value of future net cash inflows / initial investment outlay
inputs: Future net cash inflows: cash flows after the initial date, discounted on a consistent basis.
Initial investment outlay: a positive initial investment denominator.
scope: This common convention assumes one initial outlay and compatible future net inflows. Multiple outlays and other conventions need explicit treatment. The source’s cash-inflows shorthand must not ignore later operating outflows.

name: Gross profit: corresponding cost-of-sales basis
expression: Revenue − corresponding cost of goods sold
inputs: Revenue: the recognized revenue of the output sold.
Cost of goods sold: corresponding cost under the applicable accounting basis.
scope: Cost of goods sold need not equal direct costs alone. Match the revenue and cost period and scope.

name: Gross profit margin: corresponding sales basis
units: fraction; multiply by 100 for percentage display
inputs: Gross profit: matching revenue less cost of goods sold.
Revenue: the same period and sales perimeter.
scope: A zero denominator is undefined. Gross profit is an amount; gross margin is a ratio. This is distinct from unit contribution.

name: Contribution margin per unit
inputs: Unit price: selling price of the defined unit.
Unit variable cost: all relevant variable costs on the same unit basis.
scope: State which production, selling and marketing costs vary with output. Do not mix period totals with unit amounts or assume all direct costs are variable.

name: Contribution-margin ratio
expression: Contribution margin per unit / unit price
units: fraction; multiply by 100 for percentage display
inputs: Contribution margin per unit: unit price less unit variable cost.
Unit price: the matching nonzero selling price.
scope: The source uses a dash where an equals sign would be expected. Keep the unit bases compatible; this is not the same cost boundary as gross margin.

name: Consensus-trend signal: incomplete source model
inputs: Current consensus mean; consensus mean one month earlier; price.
scope: The source does not define consensus population, forecast horizon, price date, units or an evidence-backed prediction role.

name: Flash-trend signal: incomplete source model
inputs: Current six-week flash mean; its one-month-earlier comparison; price.
scope: The flash measure, overlapping windows, observation timing and scaling are not sufficiently defined for a reproducible signal.

name: Stock-return expression: undefined predictor terms
inputs: Consensus predictor; flash; controversy; neglect.
scope: No coefficients, data definitions, return period, scaling or model provenance are supplied. The expression must not be presented as a functioning return predictor.

name: Neglect signal: undefined logarithmic convention
inputs: Number of fiscal-year-one analysts; logarithm base and observation date.
scope: The source gives −Log(1 + analyst count), but does not define the base, inclusion criteria, timing or validated role in the stock-return model.

name: Two-asset volatility-balancing relation
expression: Stock weight × stock volatility = bond weight × bond volatility
inputs: Stock and bond weights: compatible allocation fractions.
Volatilities: measured or estimated on the same horizon and frequency.
scope: This is the limited relation supplied in the notes, not a complete multi-asset risk-parity or optimization model. Specify the return/volatility estimates, covariance assumptions, leverage and constraints before drawing allocation conclusions. It is not a recommended stock/bond mix.
